Where am I?
This isn’t the[school]’s storage room.

Teaching is hard work, you know?
In fact, just the other day, I was thinking-
: Yuu, are you in-
A girl appears in front of me.
She has one less dimension than the girls I usually deal with.
I’m not sure how to handle this.
: Who...are you?
: Are you a new teacher here? Your uniform doesn't match our colors.
: I don’t think so. I just kind of woke up here.

: I’m not really sure if I know the name of the[school], now that I think about it...
: You don’t know the name of your own[school]?

: Hey, you didn't...by any chance see a boy around my age in here, did you?
: Uhh, no. I only woke up a minute or two before you opened the door.
: Is he your boyfriend or something like that?
: W-What? No! Nothing like that. He’s...just a friend.
: Don’t give me that. Your true feelings are written all over your face.
: They are not!
: They definitely are...
The girl pauses for a moment before sighing to herself and spilling her 'secret' to a perfect stranger.
: Okay...So, he’s not my boyfriend...
: But he’s someone I like very much.
: We’ve known each other for a long time now, and he can be kind of strange at times...but he has a good heart.
: I see.
: How about you?
: Is there anyone you like?

: Hmm...I don’t think so.
: After all, you’re going to be going back home in a little while, aren’t you? To...Kumon-mi or whatever you called it?
: That’s right...
: I need to...get back...
But how do I even get there?
And what will happen once I do?
I have this creeping feeling that things are going to get even more confusing after this.
But then again-
This is probably just another dream.
Every time things get weird or scary-
They always go away shortly after.
Sure, they might come rushing back in the next time I’m thrown into an uncomfortable situation, but...
But that’s something I’ve learned to deal with.
And that’s something I feel like I’ll have to continue dealing with if I want to make the most of the new life I’ve been given.
And so-
I’m sure I’ll find my way back.
I’m sure.
